perspective:
From Brandon Talayumptewa’s perspective:

- I am an insurance agent. I met Benjamin Erickson professionally when he sought business insurance advice. I was aware he had limited formal education and worried about explaining complex insurance clearly.
- First meeting: Benjamin said he wanted comprehensive coverage but some terms were new. I explained liability insurance as a safety net and gave a slip-and-fall example. I explained asset protection as guarding inventory/equipment. Benjamin said it made sense, asked for an example, said it simplified things, asked about assets, and thanked me.
- Later meeting: Based on our previous interactions, I revised my belief that Benjamin could handle detailed information and felt confident going deeper. Benjamin said he was ready and had been reading up. I explained business interruption insurance and property insurance, including theft. Benjamin said BI sounded crucial in unpredictable times and comprehensive coverage was reassuring.
- Lunch meeting: I felt insecure about how Benjamin perceived my cautious nature and tried to balance detail with engaging delivery. I told him I worry about getting too detailed but want our discussions interesting. Benjamin said he appreciates thoroughness and enjoys lighter moments. I told a joke about an entrepreneur insuring his taste buds for $1 million. Benjamin was fascinated, said it made sense given the stakes, and said it was less unusual but equally important. I related it to assessing risks for his business.
- Afterward: Pleased by his positive response, I offered extra support beyond insurance. I suggested strategic investments to lower premiums, such as upgrading security systems to protect assets and reduce insurance costs. Benjamin said he was all ears, called my insights invaluable, said it sounded smart, called it a win-win, and agreed to explore further.
- Joint venture: Encouraged by our rapport and mutual benefits, I proposed co-developing a platform integrating risk management with financial planning for entrepreneurs. Benjamin agreed, asked what I had in mind, called it groundbreaking, said combining expertise could set us apart, and suggested drafting initial plans.
